title: New aether sink model for gravity

text: A Study of Non-Singular Bounce in Myrzakulov-type $f(R,T)$ Gravity with Chaplygin Gas. Khandro K Chokyi, Abdel Nasser Tawfik, Surajit Chattopadhyay. 2026. arXiv:2604.21415.
title: A Study of Non-Singular Bounce in Myrzakulov-type $f(R,T)$ Gravity with Chaplygin Gas

text: This study investigates the non-singular bounce within the framework of Myrzakulov-type $f(R,T) = R + αT + βT^2$ gravity by adopting a Chaplygin gas equation of state. We employ two methodologies: a reconstruction scheme via a symmetric scale factor ansatz (Model I) and an autonomous dynamical system analysis (Model II). Our results indicate that the quadratic trace parameter $β$ acts as a primary physical driver; specifically, for $β< 0$, the matter-geometry coupling generates sufficient geometric repulsion to effectively violate the Null Energy Condition (NEC) at high densities without the requirement of exotic matter fields. A numerical scan of the $(β, ρ_0)$ parameter space indicates a critical density threshold required to initiate the bounce, below which the Universe follows a singular General Relativity trajectory. The models are shown to be physically viable, with the effective equation of state asymptotically approaching a de Sitter attractor ($w_{\text{eff}} \to -1$) and the squared speed of sound remaining within the stability and causality bounds ($0 \le c_s^2 \le 1$). This study shows that the $f(R,T)$ framework provides a stable, classically geometric alternative to the Big Bang singularity, consistent with both early-universe requirements and late-time accelerated expansion.
title: A Study of Non-Singular Bounce in Myrzakulov-type $f(R,T)$ Gravity with Chaplygin Gas

text: Este estudio investiga el rebote no singular en el marco de la gravedad $f(R,T) = R + αT + βT^2$ de tipo Myrzakulov adoptando una ecuación de estado de gas de Chaplygin. Empleamos dos metodologías: un esquema de reconstrucción mediante un ansatz de factor de escala simétrico (Modelo I) y un análisis de sistema dinámico autónomo (Modelo II). Nuestros resultados indican que el parámetro cuadrático de la traza $β$ actúa como motor físico principal; en concreto, para $β< 0$, el acoplamiento materia-geometría genera suficiente repulsión geométrica para violar de forma efectiva la condición de energía nula (NEC) a altas densidades sin necesidad de campos de materia exótica. Un barrido numérico del espacio de parámetros $(β, ρ_0)$ indica un umbral de densidad crítica necesario para iniciar el rebote, por debajo del cual el Universo sigue una trayectoria singular de Relatividad General. Se muestra que los modelos son físicamente viables, con la ecuación de estado efectiva aproximándose asintóticamente a un atractor de de Sitter ($w_{\text{eff}} \to -1$) y el cuadrado de la velocidad del sonido manteniéndose dentro de los límites de estabilidad y causalidad ($0 \le c_s^2 \le 1$). Este estudio muestra que el marco $f(R,T)$ proporciona una alternativa estable y clásicamente geométrica a la singularidad del Big Bang, compatible tanto con los requisitos del universo primitivo como con la expansión acelerada tardía.
title: A Study of Non-Singular Bounce in Myrzakulov-type $f(R,T)$ Gravity with Chaplygin Gas

text: Cette étude examine le rebond non singulier dans le cadre de la gravité $f(R,T) = R + αT + βT^2$ de type Myrzakulov en adoptant une équation d'état de gaz de Chaplygin. Nous employons deux méthodologies : un schéma de reconstruction via un ansatz de facteur d'échelle symétrique (Modèle I) et une analyse de système dynamique autonome (Modèle II). Nos résultats indiquent que le paramètre quadratique de la trace $β$ agit comme moteur physique principal ; plus précisément, pour $β< 0$, le couplage matière-géométrie engendre une répulsion géométrique suffisante pour violer effectivement la condition d'énergie nulle (NEC) à haute densité sans nécessiter de champs de matière exotique. Un balayage numérique de l'espace des paramètres $(β, ρ_0)$ indique un seuil de densité critique requis pour déclencher le rebond, en dessous duquel l'Univers suit une trajectoire singulière de Relativité Générale. Les modèles s'avèrent physiquement viables, l'équation d'état effective tendant asymptotiquement vers un attracteur de de Sitter ($w_{\text{eff}} \to -1$) et le carré de la vitesse du son restant dans les limites de stabilité et de causalité ($0 \le c_s^2 \le 1$). Cette étude montre que le cadre $f(R,T)$ fournit une alternative stable et classiquement géométrique à la singularité du Big Bang, compatible à la fois avec les exigences de l'univers primordial et avec l'expansion accélérée tardive.
title: A Study of Non-Singular Bounce in Myrzakulov-type $f(R,T)$ Gravity with Chaplygin Gas

text: Catenoid Inspired Hyperbolic Wormhole Geometry. Bikramarka S Choudhury, Md Khalid Hossain, Farook Rahaman. 2025. Phys. Lett. B 871 (2025) 139986.
title: Catenoid Inspired Hyperbolic Wormhole Geometry

text: We unveil a novel class of traversable wormholes exhibiting exact spherical symmetry, geometrically inspired by the minimal surface structure of a catenoid. Introducing the spacetime metric, we rigorously derive its fundamental curvature properties, including the Riemann curvature tensor, and consequently compute the Einstein tensor and stress-energy tensor. This framework reveals that the wormhole is sustained by an anisotropic fluid. A detailed analysis of the energy conditions demonstrates the requisite presence of exotic matter, establishing the physical viability and constraints of this configuration. Subsequent investigations address the wormhole's traversability characteristics, gravitational lensing signatures, and dynamic stability. Crucially, we establish that this catenoid-inspired spacetime represents a finite wormhole, possessing bounded spatial extent.
title: Catenoid Inspired Hyperbolic Wormhole Geometry

text: Presentamos una nueva clase de agujeros de gusano atravesables con simetría esférica exacta, inspirados geométricamente en la estructura de superficie mínima de un catenoide. Introduciendo la métrica del espaciotiempo, derivamos rigurosamente sus propiedades de curvatura fundamentales, incluido el tensor de curvatura de Riemann, y calculamos en consecuencia el tensor de Einstein y el tensor energía-momento. Este marco revela que el agujero de gusano está sostenido por un fluido anisótropo. Un análisis detallado de las condiciones de energía demuestra la presencia necesaria de materia exótica, estableciendo la viabilidad física y las restricciones de esta configuración. Investigaciones posteriores abordan las características de atravesabilidad del agujero de gusano, sus firmas de lente gravitacional y su estabilidad dinámica. Fundamentalmente, establecemos que este espaciotiempo inspirado en el catenoide representa un agujero de gusano finito, con extensión espacial acotada.
title: Catenoid Inspired Hyperbolic Wormhole Geometry

text: Nous dévoilons une nouvelle classe de trous de ver traversables à symétrie sphérique exacte, géométriquement inspirés de la structure de surface minimale d'un caténoïde. En introduisant la métrique de l'espace-temps, nous dérivons rigoureusement ses propriétés de courbure fondamentales, dont le tenseur de courbure de Riemann, et calculons en conséquence le tenseur d'Einstein et le tenseur énergie-impulsion. Ce cadre révèle que le trou de ver est soutenu par un fluide anisotrope. Une analyse détaillée des conditions d'énergie démontre la présence nécessaire de matière exotique, établissant la viabilité physique et les contraintes de cette configuration. Des études ultérieures portent sur les caractéristiques de traversabilité du trou de ver, ses signatures de lentille gravitationnelle et sa stabilité dynamique. Point crucial, nous établissons que cet espace-temps inspiré du caténoïde représente un trou de ver fini, d'extension spatiale bornée.
title: Catenoid Inspired Hyperbolic Wormhole Geometry

text: Born Geometry, Metaparticles, and an Effective Geometric Realization of the Modular Black-Hole Remnant: A Phase-Space Resolution of the Schwarzschild Singularity. Paul-Robert Chouha. 2026. arXiv:2608.26413.
title: Born Geometry, Metaparticles, and an Effective Geometric Realization of the Modular Black-Hole Remnant: A Phase-Space Resolution of the Schwarzschild Singularity

text: Recent work on metaparticle black-hole thermodynamics suggested the existence of a finite evaporation endpoint characterized by a minimal horizon area, a maximal Hawking temperature, and a stable cold modular remnant. However, the corresponding spacetime geometry remained unknown. In this work we construct an effective geometric realization of the modular remnant within the framework of Born geometry, modular spacetime, and metaparticle dynamics. Starting from a doubled phase-space description in which spacetime coordinates are supplemented by dual coordinates, we derive a Born-doubled Schwarzschild geometry governed by a Born-invariant radial distance. The associated modular uncertainty relation prevents arbitrary localization at the phase-space origin, rendering the classical Schwarzschild singularity physically inaccessible and replacing it with a finite modular core. We then incorporate the metaparticle duality constraint, which induces an effective conformal deformation of the Born-geometric background and generates a nontrivial effective stress-energy tensor. The resulting interior region develops a finite anisotropic source characterized by a tension-dominated radial sector. Localized violations of the radial Null Energy Condition and the Strong Energy Condition arise naturally near the modular core, providing a mechanism through which the focusing assumptions underlying the Hawking--Penrose singularity theorems are evaded. These results establish an effective geometric counterpart of the modular remnant inferred from metaparticle black-hole thermodynamics and suggest that the Schwarzschild singularity is replaced by a finite Born-geometric phase-space structure whose ultraviolet behavior is governed by dual, non-geometric degrees of freedom.
title: Born Geometry, Metaparticles, and an Effective Geometric Realization of the Modular Black-Hole Remnant: A Phase-Space Resolution of the Schwarzschild Singularity

text: Trabajos recientes sobre la termodinámica de agujeros negros de metapartículas sugirieron la existencia de un punto final de evaporación finito caracterizado por un área de horizonte mínima, una temperatura de Hawking máxima y un remanente modular frío y estable. Sin embargo, la geometría del espaciotiempo correspondiente seguía siendo desconocida. En este trabajo construimos una realización geométrica efectiva del remanente modular en el marco de la geometría de Born, el espaciotiempo modular y la dinámica de metapartículas. Partiendo de una descripción en un espacio de fases duplicado en la que las coordenadas del espaciotiempo se complementan con coordenadas duales, derivamos una geometría de Schwarzschild duplicada de Born gobernada por una distancia radial invariante de Born. La relación de incertidumbre modular asociada impide una localización arbitraria en el origen del espacio de fases, lo que hace físicamente inaccesible la singularidad clásica de Schwarzschild y la sustituye por un núcleo modular finito. A continuación incorporamos la ligadura de dualidad de metapartículas, que induce una deformación conforme efectiva del fondo geométrico de Born y genera un tensor de energía-tensión efectivo no trivial. La región interior resultante desarrolla una fuente anisótropa finita caracterizada por un sector radial dominado por la tensión. Cerca del núcleo modular surgen de forma natural violaciones localizadas de la condición de energía nula radial y de la condición de energía fuerte, lo que proporciona un mecanismo mediante el cual se eluden las hipótesis de focalización en las que se basan los teoremas de singularidad de Hawking--Penrose. Estos resultados establecen una contrapartida geométrica efectiva del remanente modular inferido de la termodinámica de agujeros negros de metapartículas y sugieren que la singularidad de Schwarzschild se sustituye por una estructura finita de espacio de fases geométrica de Born cuyo comportamiento ultravioleta está gobernado por grados de libertad duales no geométricos.
title: Born Geometry, Metaparticles, and an Effective Geometric Realization of the Modular Black-Hole Remnant: A Phase-Space Resolution of the Schwarzschild Singularity

text: Des travaux récents sur la thermodynamique des trous noirs de métaparticules ont suggéré l'existence d'un point final d'évaporation fini caractérisé par une aire d'horizon minimale, une température de Hawking maximale et un résidu modulaire froid et stable. Cependant, la géométrie d'espace-temps correspondante restait inconnue. Dans ce travail, nous construisons une réalisation géométrique effective du résidu modulaire dans le cadre de la géométrie de Born, de l'espace-temps modulaire et de la dynamique des métaparticules. En partant d'une description dans un espace des phases doublé où les coordonnées d'espace-temps sont complétées par des coordonnées duales, nous dérivons une géométrie de Schwarzschild doublée de Born régie par une distance radiale invariante de Born. La relation d'incertitude modulaire associée empêche une localisation arbitraire à l'origine de l'espace des phases, rendant la singularité classique de Schwarzschild physiquement inaccessible et la remplaçant par un cœur modulaire fini. Nous incorporons ensuite la contrainte de dualité des métaparticules, qui induit une déformation conforme effective du fond géométrique de Born et génère un tenseur énergie-contrainte effectif non trivial. La région intérieure résultante développe une source anisotrope finie caractérisée par un secteur radial dominé par la tension. Des violations localisées de la condition d'énergie nulle radiale et de la condition d'énergie forte apparaissent naturellement près du cœur modulaire, fournissant un mécanisme par lequel les hypothèses de focalisation sous-jacentes aux théorèmes de singularité de Hawking--Penrose sont contournées. Ces résultats établissent une contrepartie géométrique effective du résidu modulaire déduit de la thermodynamique des trous noirs de métaparticules et suggèrent que la singularité de Schwarzschild est remplacée par une structure finie d'espace des phases géométrique de Born dont le comportement ultraviolet est régi par des degrés de liberté duaux non géométriques.
title: Born Geometry, Metaparticles, and an Effective Geometric Realization of the Modular Black-Hole Remnant: A Phase-Space Resolution of the Schwarzschild Singularity

text: Warp Drives and Martel-Poisson charts. Abhishek Chowdhury. 2024. arXiv:2404.15948.
title: Warp Drives and Martel-Poisson charts

text: We extend the construction of Alcubierre-Natário class of warp drives to an infinite class of spacetimes with similar properties. This is achieved by utilising the Martel-Poisson charts which closely resembles the Weak Painlevé-Gullstrand form for various background metrics (Mink, AdS, dS). The highlight of this construction is the non-flat intrinsic metric which in three dimensional spacetimes introduce conical singularities at the origin and in higher dimensions generates non-zero Ricci scalar for the spatial hypersurfaces away from the origin. We analyse the expansion/contraction of space and the (NEC) violations associated with these warp drives and find interesting scalings due to the global imprints of the conical defects. Other properties like tilting of light cones, event horizons and several generalisations are also discussed.
title: Warp Drives and Martel-Poisson charts

text: Extendemos la construcción de la clase de motores de curvatura de Alcubierre-Natário a una clase infinita de espaciotiempos con propiedades similares. Esto se consigue utilizando las cartas de Martel-Poisson, que se asemejan mucho a la forma débil de Painlevé-Gullstrand para diversas métricas de fondo (Mink, AdS, dS). Lo más destacado de esta construcción es la métrica intrínseca no plana, que en espaciotiempos tridimensionales introduce singularidades cónicas en el origen y en dimensiones superiores genera un escalar de Ricci no nulo para las hipersuperficies espaciales fuera del origen. Analizamos la expansión/contracción del espacio y las violaciones de la (NEC) asociadas a estos motores de curvatura y encontramos escalados interesantes debidos a las huellas globales de los defectos cónicos. También se discuten otras propiedades como la inclinación de los conos de luz, los horizontes de sucesos y varias generalizaciones.
title: Warp Drives and Martel-Poisson charts

text: Nous étendons la construction de la classe de propulsions par distorsion d'Alcubierre-Natário à une classe infinie d'espaces-temps aux propriétés similaires. Cela est obtenu en utilisant les cartes de Martel-Poisson, qui ressemblent étroitement à la forme faible de Painlevé-Gullstrand pour diverses métriques de fond (Mink, AdS, dS). Le point fort de cette construction est la métrique intrinsèque non plate, qui dans les espaces-temps tridimensionnels introduit des singularités coniques à l'origine et en dimensions supérieures engendre un scalaire de Ricci non nul pour les hypersurfaces spatiales hors de l'origine. Nous analysons l'expansion/contraction de l'espace et les violations de la (NEC) associées à ces propulsions par distorsion et trouvons des lois d'échelle intéressantes dues aux empreintes globales des défauts coniques. D'autres propriétés comme l'inclinaison des cônes de lumière, les horizons des événements et plusieurs généralisations sont également discutées.
title: Warp Drives and Martel-Poisson charts

text: Study of Wormhole in $f(Q)$ gravity with some dark energy models. Tanmoy Chowdhury, Prabir Rudra, Tandrima Chowdhury, Farook Rahaman. 2025. Annals of Physics 480 (2025) 170108.
title: Study of Wormhole in $f(Q)$ gravity with some dark energy models

text: This study discusses the development of some particular static wormhole models in the background of an extended $f(Q)$ gravity theory. Wormhole solutions are derived by considering the radial pressure to admit an equation of state corresponding to Chaplygin gas. The Chaplygin gas equation of state is taken into consideration in two different forms: $p_{r}=-\frac{Bb(r)^{u}}{ρ^{a}}$, $p_{r}=-\frac{B}{ρ^{a}}$. Wormhole models are also generated assuming that a variable barotropic fluid may explain the radial pressure given by $p_{r} =-ωρb(r)^u$. For every model, the shape function $b(r)$ is the function that can be derived from the wormhole metric in any scenario. The stability analysis of the wormhole solutions and the shape function viability for each situation are then investigated.Since each wormhole model is shown to violate the null energy condition (NEC), it can be understood that these wormholes are traversable. More generally, we investigate whether the model is stable under the hydrostatic equilibrium state condition using the TOV equation.The physical characteristics of these models are shown under the same energy circumstances. The typical characteristic is the radial pressure $p_{r}$ near the wormhole throat, which violates the NEC $(ρ+P_{r} \geq0)$. In some models, it is possible to meet the NEC at the neck and yet violate the DEC $(ρ- P_{r}\geq0)$. In summary, precise wormhole models may be generated, provided that $(ρ\geq0)$, and there may be a potential breach of the NEC at the wormhole's throat.
title: Study of Wormhole in $f(Q)$ gravity with some dark energy models

text: Este estudio discute el desarrollo de algunos modelos particulares de agujero de gusano estático en el contexto de una teoría de gravedad $f(Q)$ extendida. Las soluciones de agujero de gusano se derivan considerando que la presión radial admite una ecuación de estado correspondiente al gas de Chaplygin. La ecuación de estado del gas de Chaplygin se considera en dos formas diferentes: $p_{r}=-\frac{Bb(r)^{u}}{ρ^{a}}$, $p_{r}=-\frac{B}{ρ^{a}}$. También se generan modelos de agujero de gusano suponiendo que un fluido barotrópico variable puede explicar la presión radial dada por $p_{r} =-ωρb(r)^u$. Para cada modelo, la función de forma $b(r)$ es la función que puede derivarse de la métrica del agujero de gusano en cualquier escenario. A continuación se investigan el análisis de estabilidad de las soluciones de agujero de gusano y la viabilidad de la función de forma en cada situación. Puesto que se muestra que cada modelo de agujero de gusano viola la condición de energía nula (NEC), puede entenderse que estos agujeros de gusano son atravesables. De forma más general, investigamos si el modelo es estable bajo la condición de estado de equilibrio hidrostático utilizando la ecuación TOV. Las características físicas de estos modelos se muestran bajo las mismas circunstancias energéticas. La característica típica es la presión radial $p_{r}$ cerca de la garganta del agujero de gusano, que viola la NEC $(ρ+P_{r} \geq0)$. En algunos modelos es posible cumplir la NEC en el cuello y, sin embargo, violar la DEC $(ρ- P_{r}\geq0)$. En resumen, pueden generarse modelos de agujero de gusano precisos, siempre que $(ρ\geq0)$, y puede haber una posible violación de la NEC en la garganta del agujero de gusano.
title: Study of Wormhole in $f(Q)$ gravity with some dark energy models

text: Cette étude discute du développement de certains modèles particuliers de trous de ver statiques dans le cadre d'une théorie de gravité $f(Q)$ étendue. Les solutions de trou de ver sont dérivées en considérant que la pression radiale admet une équation d'état correspondant au gaz de Chaplygin. L'équation d'état du gaz de Chaplygin est considérée sous deux formes différentes : $p_{r}=-\frac{Bb(r)^{u}}{ρ^{a}}$, $p_{r}=-\frac{B}{ρ^{a}}$. Des modèles de trou de ver sont également générés en supposant qu'un fluide barotrope variable peut expliquer la pression radiale donnée par $p_{r} =-ωρb(r)^u$. Pour chaque modèle, la fonction de forme $b(r)$ est la fonction qui peut être dérivée de la métrique du trou de ver dans tout scénario. L'analyse de stabilité des solutions de trou de ver et la viabilité de la fonction de forme pour chaque situation sont ensuite étudiées. Comme on montre que chaque modèle de trou de ver viole la condition d'énergie nulle (NEC), on peut comprendre que ces trous de ver sont traversables. Plus généralement, nous étudions si le modèle est stable sous la condition d'état d'équilibre hydrostatique à l'aide de l'équation TOV. Les caractéristiques physiques de ces modèles sont présentées dans les mêmes circonstances énergétiques. La caractéristique typique est la pression radiale $p_{r}$ près de la gorge du trou de ver, qui viole la NEC $(ρ+P_{r} \geq0)$. Dans certains modèles, il est possible de satisfaire la NEC au col tout en violant la DEC $(ρ- P_{r}\geq0)$. En résumé, des modèles de trou de ver précis peuvent être générés, pourvu que $(ρ\geq0)$, et il peut y avoir une violation potentielle de la NEC à la gorge du trou de ver.
title: Study of Wormhole in $f(Q)$ gravity with some dark energy models

text: Phonon dynamics in spherically-curved analog-gravity Bose–Einstein condensates. J. Austin Chunn, Ruotong Zhai, Daniel E. Sheehy. 2026. The European Physical Journal C.
title: Phonon dynamics in spherically-curved analog-gravity Bose–Einstein condensates

text: We study the low energy phonon dynamics of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) with a density profile that is equivalent, via a coordinate transformation, to phonons traveling in a \lq\lq spherical\rq\rq\ curved spacetime that realizes the Friedman-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) metric. The metric of this BEC is characterized by its curvature $κ$ and a time-depdendent scale factor $a(t)$, with an increase in the latter corresponding to an expansion of the analog FLRW universe. We study the propagation of classical phonons in such BECs, finding that a sudden change in the scale factor induces ripples in the wave motion. In addition, we study quantum phonon creation (or vacuum amplification) due to the scale-factor modification and quantify their entanglement.
title: Phonon dynamics in spherically-curved analog-gravity Bose–Einstein condensates

text: Estudiamos la dinámica de fonones de baja energía de un condensado de Bose-Einstein (BEC) con un perfil de densidad equivalente, mediante una transformación de coordenadas, a fonones que viajan en un espaciotiempo curvo «esférico» que realiza la métrica de Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW). La métrica de este BEC se caracteriza por su curvatura $κ$ y un factor de escala dependiente del tiempo $a(t)$, donde un aumento de este último corresponde a una expansión del universo FLRW análogo. Estudiamos la propagación de fonones clásicos en estos BEC y encontramos que un cambio brusco del factor de escala induce ondulaciones en el movimiento ondulatorio. Además, estudiamos la creación cuántica de fonones (o amplificación del vacío) debida a la modificación del factor de escala y cuantificamos su entrelazamiento.
title: Phonon dynamics in spherically-curved analog-gravity Bose–Einstein condensates

text: Nous étudions la dynamique des phonons de basse énergie d'un condensat de Bose-Einstein (BEC) dont le profil de densité est équivalent, par une transformation de coordonnées, à des phonons voyageant dans un espace-temps courbe « sphérique » qui réalise la métrique de Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW). La métrique de ce BEC est caractérisée par sa courbure $κ$ et un facteur d'échelle dépendant du temps $a(t)$, une augmentation de ce dernier correspondant à une expansion de l'univers FLRW analogue. Nous étudions la propagation de phonons classiques dans de tels BEC et constatons qu'un changement soudain du facteur d'échelle induit des ondulations dans le mouvement ondulatoire. De plus, nous étudions la création quantique de phonons (ou amplification du vide) due à la modification du facteur d'échelle et quantifions leur intrication.
title: Phonon dynamics in spherically-curved analog-gravity Bose–Einstein condensates

text: Wave Scattering in Spatially Inhomogeneous Currents. Semyon Churilov, Andrei Ermakov, Yury Stepanyants. 2017. Phys. Rev. D 96, 064016 (2017).
title: Wave Scattering in Spatially Inhomogeneous Currents

text: We analytically study a scattering of long linear surface waves on stationary currents in a duct (canal) of constant depth and variable width. It is assumed that the background velocity linearly increases or decreases with the longitudinal coordinate due to the gradual variation of duct width. Such a model admits analytical solution of the problem in hand, and we calculate the scattering coefficients as functions of incident wave frequency for all possible cases of sub-, super-, and trans-critical currents. For completeness we study both co-current and counter-current wave propagation in accelerating and decelerating currents. The results obtained are analysed in application to recent analog gravity experiments and shed light on the problem of hydrodynamic modelling of Hawking radiation.
title: Wave Scattering in Spatially Inhomogeneous Currents

text: Estudiamos analíticamente la dispersión de ondas superficiales lineales largas en corrientes estacionarias en un conducto (canal) de profundidad constante y anchura variable. Se supone que la velocidad de fondo aumenta o disminuye linealmente con la coordenada longitudinal debido a la variación gradual de la anchura del conducto. Este modelo admite una solución analítica del problema en cuestión, y calculamos los coeficientes de dispersión en función de la frecuencia de la onda incidente para todos los casos posibles de corrientes subcríticas, supercríticas y transcríticas. Para completar, estudiamos la propagación de ondas tanto a favor como en contra de la corriente en corrientes aceleradas y deceleradas. Los resultados obtenidos se analizan en su aplicación a experimentos recientes de gravedad análoga y arrojan luz sobre el problema de la modelización hidrodinámica de la radiación de Hawking.
title: Wave Scattering in Spatially Inhomogeneous Currents

text: Nous étudions analytiquement la diffusion d'ondes de surface linéaires longues sur des courants stationnaires dans un conduit (canal) de profondeur constante et de largeur variable. On suppose que la vitesse de fond augmente ou diminue linéairement avec la coordonnée longitudinale en raison de la variation progressive de la largeur du conduit. Un tel modèle admet une solution analytique du problème considéré, et nous calculons les coefficients de diffusion en fonction de la fréquence de l'onde incidente pour tous les cas possibles de courants sous-critiques, supercritiques et transcritiques. Par souci d'exhaustivité, nous étudions la propagation des ondes à la fois dans le sens du courant et à contre-courant dans des courants accélérés et décélérés. Les résultats obtenus sont analysés en vue de leur application à des expériences récentes de gravité analogue et éclairent le problème de la modélisation hydrodynamique du rayonnement de Hawking.
title: Wave Scattering in Spatially Inhomogeneous Currents

text: Scattering of surface shallow water waves on a draining bathtub vortex. Semyon Churilov, Yury Stepanyants. 2019. Physical Review Fluids.
title: Scattering of surface shallow water waves on a draining bathtub vortex

text: In the linear approximation we study long wave scattering on an axially symmetric flow in a shallow water basin with a drain in the center. This classical problem can be considered as a model of wave scattering on a rotating black hole. For the low frequencies analytic solutions are derived to describe both pure potential perturbations (surface gravity waves), and perturbations with nonzero potential vorticity. For moderate frequencies such solutions are obtained numerically and illustrated graphically. It is shown that there are two processes governing the dynamics of perturbations, namely, the scattering of incident gravity waves by central vortex, and the emission of gravity waves stimulated by the potential vorticity. Some aspects of their joint action are discussed.
title: Scattering of surface shallow water waves on a draining bathtub vortex

text: En la aproximación lineal estudiamos la dispersión de ondas largas en un flujo axisimétrico en una cuenca de aguas poco profundas con un sumidero en el centro. Este problema clásico puede considerarse un modelo de dispersión de ondas en un agujero negro en rotación. Para bajas frecuencias se obtienen soluciones analíticas que describen tanto perturbaciones puramente potenciales (ondas gravitatorias superficiales) como perturbaciones con vorticidad potencial no nula. Para frecuencias moderadas, tales soluciones se obtienen numéricamente y se ilustran gráficamente. Se muestra que hay dos procesos que gobiernan la dinámica de las perturbaciones, a saber, la dispersión de las ondas gravitatorias incidentes por el vórtice central y la emisión de ondas gravitatorias estimulada por la vorticidad potencial. Se discuten algunos aspectos de su acción conjunta.
title: Scattering of surface shallow water waves on a draining bathtub vortex

text: Dans l'approximation linéaire, nous étudions la diffusion d'ondes longues sur un écoulement axisymétrique dans un bassin en eau peu profonde avec un drain au centre. Ce problème classique peut être considéré comme un modèle de diffusion d'ondes sur un trou noir en rotation. Pour les basses fréquences, des solutions analytiques sont dérivées pour décrire à la fois des perturbations purement potentielles (ondes gravitationnelles de surface) et des perturbations à vorticité potentielle non nulle. Pour les fréquences modérées, de telles solutions sont obtenues numériquement et illustrées graphiquement. On montre qu'il existe deux processus gouvernant la dynamique des perturbations, à savoir la diffusion des ondes gravitationnelles incidentes par le vortex central et l'émission d'ondes gravitationnelles stimulée par la vorticité potentielle. Quelques aspects de leur action conjointe sont discutés.
title: Scattering of surface shallow water waves on a draining bathtub vortex

text: Hydrodynamic models of astrophysical wormholes: the general concept. Semyon M. Churilov, Yury A. Stepanyants. 2021. University of Southern Queensland ePrints (University of Southern Queensland).
title: Hydrodynamic models of astrophysical wormholes: the general concept

text: Hydrodynamic models of astrophysical wormholes: The general concept. Semyon Churilov, Yury Stepanyants. 2021. Physics of Fluids.
title: Hydrodynamic models of astrophysical wormholes: The general concept

text: We study hydrodynamic models of astrophysical wormholes when water waves can be amplified in the course of propagation between two critical points where wave and current speeds coincide. Such models can be realised in shallow laboratory ducts with variable width and depths. In this paper, we derive the basic set of equations for shallow water waves on the spatially variable flow in the duct of a variable cross-section and present the asymptotic analysis of solutions in the neighbourhood of the critical points. The critical points mimic either the black hole (BH) horizon if the flow transits from the subcritical to the supercritical regime, or the white hole (WH) horizon if the flow transits from the supercritical to the subcritical regime. We study then, the wave propagation in the flow with two horizons when the flow transits first the BH horizon and then the WH one. The region between the horizons mimics a wormhole in general relativity. For the sake of completeness, we also study the successive transition through WH and BH horizons. The theoretical results are illustrated by numerical calculations of wave propagation in both these arrangements. It is shown that the wave amplification after passing the active zone between the horizons takes place in BH{WH arrangements only and can occur for different relationships between the subcritical and supercritical flow velocities. The frequency dependence of the amplification factor is obtained and quantified in terms of the velocity ratio within and outside the \wormhole domain". In the next paper, we plan to present exact solutions for the specific velocity profile.
title: Hydrodynamic models of astrophysical wormholes: The general concept

text: Estudiamos modelos hidrodinámicos de agujeros de gusano astrofísicos en los que las ondas de agua pueden amplificarse durante su propagación entre dos puntos críticos donde coinciden las velocidades de la onda y de la corriente. Tales modelos pueden realizarse en conductos poco profundos de laboratorio con anchura y profundidad variables. En este artículo deducimos el conjunto básico de ecuaciones para ondas de aguas poco profundas sobre el flujo espacialmente variable en un conducto de sección variable y presentamos el análisis asintótico de las soluciones en el entorno de los puntos críticos. Los puntos críticos imitan el horizonte de un agujero negro (BH) si el flujo pasa del régimen subcrítico al supercrítico, o el horizonte de un agujero blanco (WH) si el flujo pasa del régimen supercrítico al subcrítico. Estudiamos después la propagación de ondas en el flujo con dos horizontes cuando el flujo atraviesa primero el horizonte BH y luego el WH. Para ser completos, estudiamos también la transición sucesiva por los horizontes WH y BH. Los resultados teóricos se ilustran con cálculos numéricos de la propagación de ondas en ambas configuraciones. Se muestra que la amplificación de las ondas tras atravesar la zona activa entre los horizontes tiene lugar solo en las configuraciones BH-WH y puede ocurrir para distintas relaciones entre las velocidades del flujo subcrítico y supercrítico. Se obtiene la dependencia con la frecuencia del factor de amplificación y se cuantifica en función de la razón de velocidades dentro y fuera del «dominio del agujero de gusano». En el siguiente artículo planeamos presentar soluciones exactas para un perfil de velocidad concreto.
title: Hydrodynamic models of astrophysical wormholes: The general concept

text: Nous étudions des modèles hydrodynamiques de trous de ver astrophysiques dans lesquels les ondes de surface de l'eau peuvent être amplifiées au cours de leur propagation entre deux points critiques où les vitesses de l'onde et du courant coïncident. De tels modèles peuvent être réalisés dans des conduits de laboratoire peu profonds de largeur et de profondeur variables. Dans cet article, nous établissons l'ensemble de base des équations pour les ondes en eau peu profonde sur l'écoulement spatialement variable dans un conduit de section variable et présentons l'analyse asymptotique des solutions au voisinage des points critiques. Les points critiques miment soit l'horizon d'un trou noir (BH) si l'écoulement passe du régime sous-critique au régime supercritique, soit l'horizon d'un trou blanc (WH) si l'écoulement passe du régime supercritique au régime sous-critique. Nous étudions ensuite la propagation des ondes dans l'écoulement à deux horizons lorsque l'écoulement franchit d'abord l'horizon BH puis l'horizon WH. Par souci d'exhaustivité, nous étudions aussi la transition successive par les horizons WH et BH. Les résultats théoriques sont illustrés par des calculs numériques de la propagation des ondes dans ces deux configurations. Il est montré que l'amplification des ondes après traversée de la zone active entre les horizons n'a lieu que dans les configurations BH-WH et peut se produire pour différents rapports entre les vitesses d'écoulement sous-critique et supercritique. La dépendance en fréquence du facteur d'amplification est obtenue et quantifiée en fonction du rapport des vitesses à l'intérieur et à l'extérieur du « domaine du trou de ver ». Dans le prochain article, nous prévoyons de présenter des solutions exactes pour un profil de vitesse particulier.
title: Hydrodynamic models of astrophysical wormholes: The general concept

text: New Chiral Gravity. Luca Ciambelli, Stéphane Detournay, Antoine Somerhausen. 2020. Phys. Rev. D 102, 106017 (2020).
title: New Chiral Gravity

text: The phase space of three-dimensional gravity with Compere-Song-Strominger (CSS) boundary conditions is endowed with asymptotic symmetries consisting in the semi-direct product of a Virasoro and a $\hat{u}(1)$ Kač-Moody algebra, and contains BTZ black holes whose entropy can be accounted for by the degeneracy of states of a Warped CFT. By embedding these boundary conditions in Topologically Massive Gravity, we observe the existence of two special points in the space of couplings parameterized by the AdS$_3$ radius $\ell$ and the Chern-Simons coupling $μ$. When $μ= \pm {1\over \ell}$, the asymptotic symmetries reduce to either a chiral Virasoro algebra or a pure $\hat{u}(1)$ Kač-Moody current algebra. At those points, black holes have positive energy while that of linearized excitations are non-negative.
title: New Chiral Gravity

text: El espacio de fases de la gravedad tridimensional con condiciones de contorno de Compere-Song-Strominger (CSS) está dotado de simetrías asintóticas que consisten en el producto semidirecto de un álgebra de Virasoro y un álgebra de Kač-Moody $\hat{u}(1)$, y contiene agujeros negros BTZ cuya entropía puede explicarse mediante la degeneración de estados de una CFT alabeada (Warped CFT). Al incorporar estas condiciones de contorno en la gravedad topológicamente masiva, observamos la existencia de dos puntos especiales en el espacio de acoplamientos parametrizado por el radio de AdS$_3$ $\ell$ y el acoplamiento de Chern-Simons $μ$. Cuando $μ= \pm {1\over \ell}$, las simetrías asintóticas se reducen a un álgebra de Virasoro quiral o a un álgebra de corrientes de Kač-Moody $\hat{u}(1)$ pura. En esos puntos, los agujeros negros tienen energía positiva, mientras que la de las excitaciones linealizadas es no negativa.
title: New Chiral Gravity

text: L'espace des phases de la gravité tridimensionnelle avec les conditions aux limites de Compere-Song-Strominger (CSS) est doté de symétries asymptotiques constituées du produit semi-direct d'une algèbre de Virasoro et d'une algèbre de Kač-Moody $\hat{u}(1)$, et contient des trous noirs BTZ dont l'entropie peut s'expliquer par la dégénérescence des états d'une CFT gauchie (Warped CFT). En plongeant ces conditions aux limites dans la gravité topologiquement massive, nous observons l'existence de deux points particuliers dans l'espace des couplages paramétré par le rayon d'AdS$_3$ $\ell$ et le couplage de Chern-Simons $μ$. Lorsque $μ= \pm {1\over \ell}$, les symétries asymptotiques se réduisent soit à une algèbre de Virasoro chirale, soit à une algèbre de courants de Kač-Moody $\hat{u}(1)$ pure. En ces points, les trous noirs ont une énergie positive, tandis que celle des excitations linéarisées est non négative.
title: New Chiral Gravity

text: Quantum backreaction in an analog black hole. G. Ciliberto, R. Balbinot, A. Fabbri, N. Pavloff. 2025. Physical Review A 112, 063323 (2025).
title: Quantum backreaction in an analog black hole

text: We extend the Gross-Pitaevskii equation to incorporate the effect of quantum fluctuations onto the flow of a weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensate. Applying this framework to an analog black hole in a quasi-one-dimensional, transonic flow, we investigate how acoustic Hawking radiation back-reacts on the background condensate. Our results point to the emergence of stationary density and velocity undulations in the supersonic region (analogous to the black hole interior) and enable to evaluate the change in upstream and downstream Mach numbers caused by Hawking radiation. These findings provide new insight into the interplay between quantum fluctuations and analog gravity in Bose-Einstein condensates.
title: Quantum backreaction in an analog black hole

text: Extendemos la ecuación de Gross-Pitaevskii para incorporar el efecto de las fluctuaciones cuánticas sobre el flujo de un condensado de Bose-Einstein débilmente interactuante. Aplicando este marco a un agujero negro análogo en un flujo transónico cuasiunidimensional, investigamos cómo la radiación de Hawking acústica ejerce una retroacción sobre el condensado de fondo. Nuestros resultados apuntan a la aparición de ondulaciones estacionarias de densidad y de velocidad en la región supersónica (análoga al interior del agujero negro) y permiten evaluar el cambio en los números de Mach aguas arriba y aguas abajo causado por la radiación de Hawking. Estos resultados aportan una nueva perspectiva sobre la interacción entre las fluctuaciones cuánticas y la gravedad análoga en los condensados de Bose-Einstein.
title: Quantum backreaction in an analog black hole

text: Nous étendons l'équation de Gross-Pitaevskii afin d'incorporer l'effet des fluctuations quantiques sur l'écoulement d'un condensat de Bose-Einstein faiblement interagissant. En appliquant ce cadre à un trou noir analogue dans un écoulement transsonique quasi unidimensionnel, nous étudions la manière dont le rayonnement de Hawking acoustique rétroagit sur le condensat de fond. Nos résultats indiquent l'apparition d'ondulations stationnaires de densité et de vitesse dans la région supersonique (analogue à l'intérieur du trou noir) et permettent d'évaluer la variation des nombres de Mach en amont et en aval causée par le rayonnement de Hawking. Ces résultats apportent un éclairage nouveau sur l'interaction entre fluctuations quantiques et gravité analogue dans les condensats de Bose-Einstein.
title: Quantum backreaction in an analog black hole

text: Gowdy Cosmological Models from Stringy Black Holes. Tzihue Cisneros-Perez, Alfredo Herrera-Aguilar, Julio Cesar Mejia-Ambriz, Violeta Rojas-Macias. 2006. arXiv:hep-th/0603250.
title: Gowdy Cosmological Models from Stringy Black Holes

text: In the framework of 4D Einstein-Maxwell Dilaton-Axion theory we show how to obtain a family of both unpolarized and polarized S^1XS^2 Gowdy cosmological models endowed with nontrivial axion, dilaton and electromagnetic fields from a solitonic rotating black hole-type solution by interchanging the r and t coordinates in the region located between the horizons of the black hole configuration. We also get a family of Kantowski-Sachs cosmologies with topology R^1XS^2 from the polarized Gowdy cosmological models by decompactifying one of the compact dimensions.
title: Gowdy Cosmological Models from Stringy Black Holes

text: En el marco de la teoría de Einstein-Maxwell dilatón-axión en 4D mostramos cómo obtener una familia de modelos cosmológicos de Gowdy S^1XS^2, tanto no polarizados como polarizados, dotados de campos axiónico, dilatónico y electromagnético no triviales, a partir de una solución solitónica de tipo agujero negro en rotación intercambiando las coordenadas r y t en la región situada entre los horizontes de la configuración de agujero negro. También obtenemos una familia de cosmologías de Kantowski-Sachs con topología R^1XS^2 a partir de los modelos cosmológicos de Gowdy polarizados descompactificando una de las dimensiones compactas.
title: Gowdy Cosmological Models from Stringy Black Holes

text: Dans le cadre de la théorie d'Einstein-Maxwell dilaton-axion en 4D, nous montrons comment obtenir une famille de modèles cosmologiques de Gowdy S^1XS^2, non polarisés comme polarisés, dotés de champs axionique, dilatonique et électromagnétique non triviaux, à partir d'une solution solitonique de type trou noir en rotation en échangeant les coordonnées r et t dans la région située entre les horizons de la configuration de trou noir. Nous obtenons également une famille de cosmologies de Kantowski-Sachs de topologie R^1XS^2 à partir des modèles cosmologiques de Gowdy polarisés en décompactifiant l'une des dimensions compactes.
title: Gowdy Cosmological Models from Stringy Black Holes

text: Acoustic black-hole bombs and scalar clouds in a photon-fluid model. Marzena Ciszak, Francesco Marino. 2021. Phys. Rev. D 103, 045004 (2021).
title: Acoustic black-hole bombs and scalar clouds in a photon-fluid model

text: Massive bosonic fields in the background of a Kerr black hole can either trigger superradiant instabilities (black-hole bombs) or form equilibrium configurations corresponding to pure bound states, known as stationary scalar clouds. Here, similar phenomena are shown to emerge in the fluctuation dynamics of a rotating photon-fluid model. In the presence of suitable vortex flows, the density fluctuations are governed by the massive Klein-Gordon equation on a (2+1) curved spacetime, possessing an ergoregion and an event horizon. We report on superradiant instabilities originating from quasi-bound phonon states trapped by the vortex background and, remarkably, on the existence of stationary modes in synchronous rotation with the horizon. These represent the acoustic counterpart of astrophysical scalar clouds. Our system offers a promising platform for analogue gravity experiments on superradiant instabilities of massive bosons and black-hole-field equilibrium configurations.
title: Acoustic black-hole bombs and scalar clouds in a photon-fluid model

text: Los campos bosónicos masivos en el fondo de un agujero negro de Kerr pueden desencadenar inestabilidades superradiantes (bombas de agujero negro) o formar configuraciones de equilibrio correspondientes a estados ligados puros, conocidas como nubes escalares estacionarias. Aquí se muestra que fenómenos similares surgen en la dinámica de fluctuaciones de un modelo de fluido de fotones en rotación. En presencia de flujos de vórtice adecuados, las fluctuaciones de densidad están gobernadas por la ecuación de Klein-Gordon masiva en un espaciotiempo curvo de (2+1) dimensiones que posee una ergorregión y un horizonte de sucesos. Informamos sobre inestabilidades superradiantes originadas por estados de fonones cuasiligados atrapados por el fondo de vórtice y, notablemente, sobre la existencia de modos estacionarios en rotación síncrona con el horizonte. Estos representan la contrapartida acústica de las nubes escalares astrofísicas. Nuestro sistema ofrece una plataforma prometedora para experimentos de gravedad análoga sobre inestabilidades superradiantes de bosones masivos y configuraciones de equilibrio agujero negro-campo.

title: Null geodesics in the Alcubierre warp drive spacetime: the view from the bridge

text: The null geodesic equations in the Alcubierre warp drive spacetime are numerically integrated to determine the angular deflection and redshift of photons which propagate through the distortion of the ``warp drive'' bubble to reach an observer at the origin of the warp effect. We find that for a starship with an effective warp speed exceeding the speed of light, stars in the forward hemisphere will appear closer to the direction of motion than they would to an observer at rest. This aberration is qualitatively similar to that caused by special relativity. Behind the starship, a conical region forms from within which no signal can reach the starship, an effective ``horizon''. Conversely, there is also an horizon-like structure in a conical region in front of the starship, into which the starship cannot send a signal. These causal structures are somewhat analogous to the Mach cones associated with supersonic fluid flow. The existence of these structures suggests that the divergence of quantum vacuum energy when the starship effectively exceeds the speed of light, first discovered in two dimensions, will likely be present in four dimensions also, and prevent any warp-drive starship from ever exceeding the effective speed of light.

title: Problems with Time-Varying Extra Dimensions or "Cardassian Expansion" as Alternatives to Dark Energy

text: It has recently been proposed that the Universe might be accelerating as a consequence of extra dimensions with time varying size. We show that although these scenarios can lead to acceleration, they run into serious difficulty when taking into account limits on the time variation of the four dimensional Newton's constant. On the other hand, models of ``Cardassian'' expansion based on extra dimensions which have been constructed so far violate the weak energy condition for the bulk stress energy, for parameters that give an accelerating universe.

title: What no one has seen before: gravitational waveforms from warp drive collapse

text: Despite originating in science fiction, warp drives have a concrete description in general relativity, with Alcubierre first proposing a spacetime metric that supported faster-than-light travel. Whilst there are numerous practical barriers to their implementation in real life, including a requirement for negative energy, computationally, one can simulate their evolution in time given an equation of state describing the matter. In this work, we study the signatures arising from a warp drive "containment failure", assuming a stiff equation of state for the fluid. We compute the emitted gravitational-wave signal and track the energy fluxes of the fluid. Apart from its rather speculative application to the search for extraterrestrial life in gravitational-wave detector data, this work is interesting as a study of the dynamical evolution and stability of spacetimes that violate the null energy condition. Our work highlights the importance of exploring strange new spacetimes, to (boldly) simulate what no one has seen before.

Detections of gravitational waves by the LIGO Scientific-Virgo-Kagra Collaborations [e.g.,][]LIGOScientific:2018mvr,LIGOScientific:2020ibl,KAGRA:2021vkt are paving the way to viewing extreme gravitational events across the entire visible universe. To search for such signals and to correctly identify them in the measured data, it is important to understand their phenomenology and properties. Numerical relativity (NR) is one of the main tools for computing gravitational-wave signals for spacetimes in the highly dynamical strongly gravity regime in the absence of symmetries [4, 5, 6, 7]. section: Formalism for the warp drive simulation
text:
We follow the standard numerical-relativity approach to solving the Einstein Equation

$$G_{\mu \nu}= R_{\mu \nu} - \frac{1}{2} R g_{\mu \nu} = 8 \pi T_ {\mu \nu} \tag{1}$$

as an initial value problem, using the $3+1$-decomposed form and setting $G=c=1$. This means that we define spacelike hypersurfaces that foliate the four-dimensional manifold, specify initial data on a particular hypersurface, and evolve it forward in our chosen time coordinate using the method of lines. 
(See the standard numerical relativity texts [39, 40, 5] for detailed discussions.)
The $3+1$-decomposed metric in coordinates adapted to the slicing takes the form

$${\rm d} s^2 = (-\alpha^2 + \beta_i \beta^i) {\rm d} t^2 + 2 \beta_i {\rm d}t {\rm d}x^i + 
\gamma_{ij} {\rm d}x^i {\rm d}x^j, \tag{2}$$

where $\alpha$ is the lapse function, $\beta^i$ is the shift vector, 
and $\gamma_{ij}$ is the spatial metric connected to the spatial hypersurface. The description is completed by the extrinsic curvature $K_{ij}$, which is roughly related to the time derivative of $\gamma_{ij}$, and more rigorously defined as its Lie derivative, such that

$$K_{ij} = - \frac{1}{2 \alpha} \partial_t \gamma_{ij} + D_{(i} \beta_{j)}. \tag{3}$$

It will also be useful to note that $n_\mu = (-\alpha, 0,0,0)$ is the normal to the spatial hypersurface.
title: What no one has seen before: gravitational waveforms from warp drive collapse

text:
Although, as discussed above, many alternatives with improved physical properties have been discussed in the literature, we will consider in this work the original Alcubierre metric [15] for which

$$\begin{aligned}\alpha & = & 1, \\
\gamma_{ij} & = & \delta_{ij}, \\
\beta^i & = & \left(0, 0, -v_s f(r_s)\right),\end{aligned} \tag{4}$$

with the quantities $r_s$ and $v_s$ defined as

$$v_s = \frac{{\rm d}z_s}{{\rm d}t}, \quad
r_s = \sqrt{x^2+y^2+(z-z_s)^2}, \tag{5}$$

and 

$$f(r_s) = \frac{\tanh(\sigma (r_s +R) )-\tanh(\sigma (r_s -R) )}{2 \tanh(\sigma R)}. \tag{6}$$

The free parameters $R$ and $\sigma$ determine the shape of the warp bubble, specifically its radius and the wall thickness $\sim 1/\sigma$. 

We will use the value of $R$ to define the system of units in which our results are expressed - our simulations have a scaling freedom that means that they apply to any similar warp drive with size $R$. Specifying the physical value of $R$ determines the other physical values of our measurements, including the gravitational-wave fluxes and the energy radiated. For reference, for a warp bubble of size $R=1$ km, the relevant quantities in physical units are $t=1[R]$ is 3.33 $\mu$s and $E$ or $M=1[R]$ is 0.677 $M_\odot$
[^3].

The initial data for the matter degrees of freedom is computed from the energy-momentum-tensor that supports the initial spacetime curvature deformation. 
We describe the state of the matter at any time in terms of projections of the stress-energy tensor

$$\begin{aligned}S_{\mu \nu} & =& P^\sigma_\mu P^\rho_\nu T_{\sigma \rho}, \\
S_\mu& = & - P^\sigma_\mu n^\rho T_{\sigma \rho}, \\
\rho & = & n^\mu n^\nu T_{\mu \nu},\end{aligned} \tag{8}$$

with the projection operator $P^\mu_\nu = \delta^\mu_\nu + n^\mu n_\nu$ where $n^\mu$ is the normal vector to the spatial hypersurface defined above. In coordinates adapted to the slicing, we can work with the ten components

$$\begin{aligned}S_{ij} & =& T_{ij}, \\
S_i& = & -\frac{1}{\alpha} T_{it} + \frac{\beta^j}{\alpha}T_{ij}, \\
\rho & = & \frac{1}{\alpha^2} T_{tt} - 2 \frac{\beta^i}{\alpha^2}T_{it} + \frac{\beta^i\beta^j}{\alpha^2}T_{ij}.\end{aligned} \tag{9}$$

Knowing that the energy-momentum-tensor has to satisfy the Einstein Equation, we can directly calculate the quantities on the right-hand side from Eq. (1) as

$$T_{\mu \nu} = \frac{1}{8 \pi} \left( R_{\mu \nu} - \frac{R}{2} g_{\mu \nu} \right), \tag{10}$$

where the Ricci tensor can be straightforwardly calculated from the Alcubierre metric in terms of derivatives of the shift.

**Figura 2.** The evolution in time of the real part of the Weyl scalar $ _4$ for the case of $v=0.1$. This quantity provides a measure of the spacetime curvature and, in the far region, can be identified with the gravitational wave content of the spacetime. In the last two panels, we see a burst of gravitational-wave radiation leaving the collapsed remnant of the warp bubble. Movie at https://youtu.be/rZsre-y4hlM?feature=shared.

For the metric evolution, we use the standard CCZ4 formulation of [42] and the moving puncture gauge [43, 44, 45, 46] within the numerical-relativity code grchombo [47, 48, 49], which uses the method of lines, with an RK4 time integration and 4th order finite difference stencils for calculating spatial gradients.

We note that for the gauge evolution we use the shock-avoiding Bona-Masso type gauge slicing originally proposed by Alcubierre [50, 51], and recently advocated for by Baumgarte and Hilditch [52] in the context of critical collapse simulations. We find that the shock-avoiding slicing gives much better stability and, more importantly, allows us to extract coherent gravitational waveforms in the wave zone, whereas in the standard gauge, we obtained large unphysical gauge effects that hindered us in extracting the physical gravitational-wave signal.

Because this gauge has a tendency to push the extrinsic curvature to zero, one should not over-interpret the evolution shown in Fig. . It quickly decays to zero in the simulation before the matter and gravitational-wave fluxes have begun to leave the volume. 

Better quantities to track the evolution of the metric curvature are the Weyl scalars, in particular $\Psi_4$. We study the tensorial gravitational-wave modes emitted by the warp drive by extracting the Newman-Penrose scalar $\Psi_4$ with the tetrads proposed by [53], projected into spin-weight $-2$ spherical harmonics, $\psi_{lm}=\oint_{S^2}\Psi_4|_{r=r_\mathrm{ex}}\left[{}_{-2}\bar{Y}^{lm}\right]\,\rmd \Omega$, 
where $\rmd \Omega = \sin\theta\,\rmd\theta\,\rmd\varphi$ is the area element on the $S^2$ unit sphere. The evolution of the real part of $\Psi_4$ is illustrated in Fig. .

**Figura 3.** The evolution in time of the matter energy density $ $ for the case of $v=0.1$. We see that a ring of positive energy forms within the initially negative energy density bubble and propels it outwards, which is reminiscent of Bondi:1957zz. There are several waves of alternating positive and negative energies. In the final panel, we see that the remnant appears stable, and compared to Fig. fig:Weyl, we see that the matter waves propagate at roughly the same speed as the gravitational waves. The requirement that $\nabla_\nu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ gives us four evolution equations for the components of the matter $\rho$ and $S_i$ as follows: 

$$\partial_t \rho = \beta^i D_i \rho - \gamma^{ij} \frac{1}{\alpha} D_j \left( \alpha^2 S_i \right) + \alpha ( S_{ij} K^{ij} + \rho K), \tag{11}$$

$$\partial_t S_i = \beta^j D_j S_i + S_j D_i \beta^j - \gamma^{jk}D_k (\alpha S_{ij}) + \alpha K S_i - \rho \partial_i \alpha. \tag{12}$$

The evolution equation for $S_{ij}$ is, in principle, free - once we specify the equation of state of the matter, it would be fully determined. We base our choice on the observation that the initial warp drive spacetime has an average pressure of [27]

$$\bar{p} \equiv \gamma^{ij} S_{ij} /3 = \rho - \frac{1}{12\pi} \nabla_a(K n^a) ~, \tag{13}$$

base our choice on the observation that the initial warp drive spacetime has an average pressure of [27]

$$\bar{p} \equiv \gamma^{ij} S_{ij} /3 = \rho - \frac{1}{12\pi} \nabla_a(K n^a) ~, \tag{13}$$

which we can reexpress using the ADM formalism as

$$\bar{p} = \frac{\rho}{3} - \frac{1}{24\pi} \left( \frac{D^2\alpha}{\alpha} + K_{ij} K^{ij} + K^2 \right) ~. \tag{14}$$

We then decompose the stress density tensor as

$$S_{ij} = \bar{p} \gamma_{ij} + \sigma_{ij} \tag{15}$$

where the second term is trace-free by construction and represents the anisotropic stress component (it is initially non-zero for the Alcubierre metric). We then impose that

$$\begin{aligned}\partial_t \sigma_{ij} &= 
\beta^k D_k \sigma_{ij} + \sigma_{kj} \partial_i \beta^k + \sigma_{ik} \partial_j \beta^k - \kappa \alpha \sigma_{ij}, \\
\partial_t \bar{p} &= 
\beta^i \partial_i \bar{p}
+ \partial_t {\rho}
- \beta^i \partial_i \rho
- \kappa \alpha (\bar{p} - \rho),\end{aligned} \tag{16}$$

where the first terms are the advection of the fields in spacetime and the terms containing $\kappa$ set a timescale related to proper time for the decay of the anisotropic stresses to zero and the pressure to that of a stiff fluid for which $\bar{p} = \rho$. We take the timescale $1/\kappa$ to be of order $[R]$.

This construction assumes that there is some transition after the warp field breakdown that reverts the warp fluid to a perfect fluid with a stiff equation of state and a velocity that matches the normal observers, such that the divergence term in Eq. (13) and the anisotropic stresses decay away. Further investigations are needed to understand the influence of the equation of state of the warp field on the gravitational-wave signal, but it appears that the metric behaviour mostly dominates the signal. However, the chosen equation of state will strongly affect the matter fluxes, which may change the conclusions in Sec. .

text:
The size of the domain is $L=168~[R]$ with $N=224$ cells on the coarsest grid in the direction of travel of the warp ship (the $z$ axis). In the $x$ and $y$ directions, we use the symmetry of the problem to halve the simulation domain so that we only evolve a quarter of the full domain, with appropriate parities at the reflection boundaries. In the nonsymmetric directions, we use Sommerfeld boundary conditions [48]. We employ 6 levels of 2:1 refinement, such that the finest grid has a width of $2.625 [R]$ and the finest grid spacing is $dx\sim 0.0117 [R]$. 

For all runs, the size of the warp ship in code units is set to be $R=1$, and the value that determines the wall thickness $\sigma$ is set to be $8$. The velocity of the warp ship is varied between 0.1 and 0.2. We have found that we can stably evolve higher velocities up to 0.5, but good quality results require very high resolutions, which would be better achieved with a code adapted to the axisymmetry. This work can be viewed as a step towards the study of the physicality of the faster-than-light case, where there are good reasons to suppose that the spacetime should be pathological in some way. By showing that numerical evolutions can be made to work at sub-light speeds, this gives us hope of being able to trace a point of breakdown near light speed.

The waves are extracted at a radius of $14[R]$.

The waves are extracted at a radius of $14[R]$. This is much smaller than values used in binary extraction, but the system here is very different and so the comparison is not appropriate. In particular, the spacetime is already flat outside the original bubble wall at $R$. The total integrated mass of the matter is also initially of order (minus) $M = \int \rho dV \sim 0.01R$, and not $M\sim R$ as in, say, a neutron star. Since the frequency of the waves is high relative to the grid spacing, we need to extract further in to obtain a good resolution of the frequencies using the adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) hierarchy. We have checked the consistency of the waves at different resolutions, and details of the checks we have done on convergence of the constraints and verification of the matter evolution are given in Appendix .

text:
A visualisation of the evolution of the gravitational-wave content is shown in Fig. . We plot the extracted Weyl scalar $\Psi_4$ for the main $m=0$ modes in Fig. . The signal comes as a burst, initially having no gravitational wave content, followed by an oscillatory period with a characteristic frequency of order $1/[R]$. Overall, the signal is very distinct from the typical compact binary coalescences observed by gravitational-wave detectors and more similar to events like the collapse of an unstable neutron star or the head-on collision of two black holes [54, 55]. However, since the remnant is not a black hole, there is no characteristic black hole ringdown in the signal, and there is evidence of a longer lower frequency tail, particularly for higher velocities.

Integrating $\Psi_4$, we find that for a warp speed of $v=0.1$, the magnitude of the strain times the radius of extraction is of order $10^{-2} [R]$. Thus, for a 1 km-sized warp ship, the strain of the signal at a distance of 1 Mpc would be $10^{-21}$. However, its frequency ($f\sim 1/[R]$) equates to $f\sim$ 300 kHz, which is outside the range of current ground based detectors. Proposals for higher frequency detectors have been made [56], so in future one may be able to put bounds on the existence of such signals.

Proposals for higher frequency detectors have been made [56], so in future one may be able to put bounds on the existence of such signals. Depending on the size of the warp bubble, which determines the frequency of the signal, as well as the distance to the source, these signatures may be detected through a coherent search or burst search combining information from multiple gravitational-wave detectors [e.g.,][]Sutton:2009gi,Cornish:2014kda,Klimenko:2015ypf. A more in depth analysis, like the one of [1], would be needed to give accurate bounds.

We note that since the matter and gravitational waves propagate at the same speed, the gravitational waves are never in an exact vacuum. We use the appropriate calculation of the Weyl scalars to account for this, but it means that the two components may continue to interact and that the gravitational waves will not fall off exactly as $1/r$ (although the difference is small over the domain we study). This is specific to the case where the matter propagates at the speed of light, whereas in a more realistic matter model we would expect the matter to be moving slower and the gravitational waves to propagate ahead. This is another point that could be investigated further in future work.

We measure the matter flux out of a spherical coordinate surface $\partial\Sigma$ with unit coordinate normal vector $s^i$ and coordinate area element $dA$ as

$$F = \int_{\partial\Sigma} \sqrt{\gamma} ~T^i_0 s_i dA \tag{17}$$

where $\gamma$ is the determinant of the spatial metric $\gamma_{ij}$ (see [2] for a derivation and details on practical implementation).
We can also integrate this to find the total energy flux that is emitted up to a time $t$ as

$$\Delta E = \int_0^t F(\tilde{t}) d\tilde{t} ~. \tag{18}$$

A visualisation of the evolution of the matter-energy density $\rho$ is shown in Fig. . In Fig. , we show a comparison of the integrated matter and gravitational-wave fluxes out of the sphere at a coordinate radius of $r=14[R]$ around the warp bubble versus time. We see that whilst the gravitational-wave flux is strictly positive as expected, the matter flux alternates in sign, with waves of positive and negative energy leaving the volume. It appears from the evolution that the ejection of matter is driven by a shell of positive energy forming within the negative energy density shell of the initial bubble and driving it outwards. This is reminiscent of the early works of [3], showing the effect of repulsion and attraction between positive and negative energy matter.

The result is that the final mass of the spacetime volume is more positive (having started at zero). text:
In this work, we proposed a formalism for studying warp drive spacetimes dynamically and produced the first fully consistent numerical-relativity waveforms for the collapse of a warp drive bubble. 

We also studied the evolution of the fluxes of matter and gravitational-wave energy from the spacetime, finding that an initial wave of negative energy matter is emitted, followed by alternating positive and negative energy waves. The gravitational-wave flux starts shortly after and is positive throughout, as expected. The end result is a net negative flux of energy, resulting in a higher final mass of the spacetime volume. It would be interesting to explore to what extent this behaviour is generic or depends on the chosen equation of state supporting the warp bubble. To do this, one would want to consistently implement a fluid description with a general rest frame velocity and equation of state, unlike the somewhat ad hoc setup employed here.

This work could be extended in several other directions. Firstly, using a code better adapted to the axisymmetry, one could extend to higher speeds, including those that exceed $v=1.0$, to see if there is a change in behaviour as light speed is approached. One might expect to see some kind of pathology develop, e.g., the formation of elliptic regions that cause the dynamical evolution to fail.
title: What no one has seen before: gravitational waveforms from warp drive collapse

text:
there is a change in behaviour as light speed is approached. One might expect to see some kind of pathology develop, e.g., the formation of elliptic regions that cause the dynamical evolution to fail. Better resolution and longer evolutions would also allow better characterization of the strain signal, particularly the role of the gravitational-wave memory content [57]. 

As discussed above, for a 1km-sized ship, the frequency of the signal $\sim 300$ kHz is much higher than the range probed by existing detectors, so current observations cannot constrain the occurrence of such events. However, the amplitude of the strain signal would be significant for any such event within our galaxy and even beyond - at a distance of 1 Mpc, slightly further than the Andromeda galaxy, the strain amplitude is similar to LIGO detector's peak sensitivity. The signal is therefore potentially within the reach of future detectors targeting higher frequencies [56]. We caution that the waveforms obtained are likely to be highly specific to the model employed, which has several known theoretical problems, as discussed in the Introduction. Further work would be required to understand how generic the signatures are, and properly characterise their detectability.

To validate our simulations, we monitor the violations of the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints which are given by

$$\begin{aligned}\mathcal{H} &:= R + \frac{2}{3}K^2 
- \tilde{A}_{kl}\tilde{A}^{kl}-2\Lambda-16\pi\rho,
\\

\mathcal{M}_i &:= \tilde{\gamma}^{kl}\left(\partial_k \tilde{A}_{li} 
-2\tilde{\Gamma}^m_{l(i}\tilde{A}_{k)m}
-3\tilde{A}_{ik}\frac{\partial_l\chi}{2\chi}\right) \\

& \quad -\frac{2}{3}\partial_iK - 8\pi S_i.\end{aligned} \tag{19}$$

In the continuum limit these two quantities should vanish. 
We check that the initial values converge to zero at the appropriate order, which validates the initial stress energy tensor components $\rho$ and $S_i$. The Hamiltonian constraint is solved exactly to numerical precision, whereas the spatial gradients in the Momentum constraint mean that it should initial converge at 4th order. During the evolution we expect errors to be dominated by the time integration, and give something between 1st and 3rd order, with some of the drop in convergence caused by the approximate way that we zero the constraints outside the volume.

We calculate the L2 norm of the constraints over the coordinate volume for which the matter integrals are evaluated (with its 2D surface also being the surface used for extraction of the gravitational waves), which is at a coordinate radius of $r=14[R]$ from the centre of the grid.
As shown in Fig , the constraint violations remain under control throughout the simulation and converge at a reasonable order.

To verify that the matter is sufficiently resolved within the volume of interest, we also reconcile the matter quantities over time, checking that the net energy flux out of the surface matches the change in the matter energy and any exchange with the curvature (often referred to as a “source”) over time. For this, we follow the approach of [2]. As shown in the last panel of Fig. , the agreement is good throughout the simulation, which gives us confidence in the matter evolution.

text: Magnonic Analogue of Black/White Hole Horizon in Superfluid $^3$He-B. M. Človečko, E. Gažo, M. Kupka, P. Skyba. 2018. Phys. Rev. Lett. 123, 161302 (2019).
title: Magnonic Analogue of Black/White Hole Horizon in Superfluid $^3$He-B

text: We report on theoretical model and experimental results of the experiment made in a limit of absolute zero temperature ($\sim$ 600\,$μ$K) studying the spin wave analogue of black/white hole horizon using spin (magnonic) superfluidity in superfluid $^3$He-B. As an experimental tool simulating the properties of the black/white horizon we used the spin-precession waves propagating on the background of the spin super-currents between two Bose-Einstein condensates of magnons in form of homogeneously precessing domains. We provide experimental evidence of the white hole formation for spin precession waves in this system, together with observation of an amplification effect. Moreover, the estimated temperature of the spontaneous Hawking radiation in this system is about four orders of magnitude lower than the system's background temperature what makes it a promising tool to study the effect of spontaneous Hawking radiation.
title: Magnonic Analogue of Black/White Hole Horizon in Superfluid $^3$He-B

text: Presentamos el modelo teórico y los resultados experimentales de un experimento realizado en el límite de temperatura de cero absoluto ($\sim$ 600\,$μ$K) que estudia el análogo en ondas de espín del horizonte de agujero negro/agujero blanco usando la superfluidez de espín (magnónica) en el superfluido $^3$He-B. Como herramienta experimental que simula las propiedades del horizonte negro/blanco usamos ondas de precesión de espín que se propagan sobre el fondo de las supercorrientes de espín entre dos condensados de Bose-Einstein de magnones en forma de dominios de precesión homogénea. Aportamos evidencia experimental de la formación de un agujero blanco para las ondas de precesión de espín en este sistema, junto con la observación de un efecto de amplificación. Además, la temperatura estimada de la radiación de Hawking espontánea en este sistema es unos cuatro órdenes de magnitud inferior a la temperatura de fondo del sistema, lo que lo convierte en una herramienta prometedora para estudiar el efecto de la radiación de Hawking espontánea.
title: Magnonic Analogue of Black/White Hole Horizon in Superfluid $^3$He-B

text: Nous présentons le modèle théorique et les résultats expérimentaux d'une expérience réalisée à la limite de la température du zéro absolu ($\sim$ 600\,$μ$K) étudiant l'analogue en ondes de spin de l'horizon de trou noir/trou blanc à l'aide de la superfluidité de spin (magnonique) dans le superfluide $^3$He-B. Comme outil expérimental simulant les propriétés de l'horizon noir/blanc, nous avons utilisé des ondes de précession de spin se propageant sur le fond des supercourants de spin entre deux condensats de Bose-Einstein de magnons sous forme de domaines en précession homogène. Nous apportons la preuve expérimentale de la formation d'un trou blanc pour les ondes de précession de spin dans ce système, ainsi que l'observation d'un effet d'amplification. De plus, la température estimée du rayonnement de Hawking spontané dans ce système est inférieure d'environ quatre ordres de grandeur à la température de fond du système, ce qui en fait un outil prometteur pour étudier l'effet du rayonnement de Hawking spontané.
title: Magnonic Analogue of Black/White Hole Horizon in Superfluid $^3$He-B

text: Magnonic Analogue Black/White Hole Horizon in Superfluid $^3$He-B: experiment. M. Človečko, E. Gažo, P. Skyba. 2019. arXiv:1904.09183.
title: Magnonic Analogue Black/White Hole Horizon in Superfluid $^3$He-B: experiment

text: We provide experimental details of the first experiment made in zero temperature limit ($\sim$ 600\,$μ$K) studying the magnonic black/white hole horizon analogue using absolutely pure physical system based on the spin superfluidity in superfluid $^3$He-B. We show that spin precession waves propagating on the background of the spin super-currents in a channel between two Bose-Einstein condensates of magnons in form of homogeneously precessing domains mimic the properties of the black/white horizon. Once the white hole horizon is formed and blocks the propagation of the spin-precession waves between two domains, we observed an amplification effect, i.e. when the energy of the spin precession waves reflected from the horizon is higher than the energy of the excited spin precession waves before horizon was formed. Moreover, the estimated temperature of the spontaneous Hawking radiation in this model system is about four orders of magnitude lower than the system's background temperature what makes it a promising tool to study the effect of spontaneous Hawking radiation.
title: Magnonic Analogue Black/White Hole Horizon in Superfluid $^3$He-B: experiment

text: Proporcionamos los detalles experimentales del primer experimento realizado en el límite de temperatura cero ($\sim$ 600\,$μ$K) que estudia el análogo magnónico de horizonte de agujero negro/blanco usando un sistema físico absolutamente puro basado en la superfluidez de espín en $^3$He-B superfluido. Mostramos que las ondas de precesión de espín que se propagan sobre el fondo de las supercorrientes de espín en un canal entre dos condensados de Bose-Einstein de magnones en forma de dominios de precesión homogénea imitan las propiedades del horizonte negro/blanco. Una vez formado el horizonte de agujero blanco, que bloquea la propagación de las ondas de precesión de espín entre los dos dominios, observamos un efecto de amplificación, es decir, la energía de las ondas de precesión de espín reflejadas en el horizonte es mayor que la energía de las ondas de precesión de espín excitadas antes de formarse el horizonte. Además, la temperatura estimada de la radiación de Hawking espontánea en este sistema modelo es unos cuatro órdenes de magnitud inferior a la temperatura de fondo del sistema, lo que lo convierte en una herramienta prometedora para estudiar el efecto de la radiación de Hawking espontánea.
title: Magnonic Analogue Black/White Hole Horizon in Superfluid $^3$He-B: experiment

text: Nous présentons les détails expérimentaux de la première expérience réalisée dans la limite de température nulle ($\sim$ 600\,$μ$K) étudiant l'analogue magnonique d'horizon de trou noir/blanc à l'aide d'un système physique absolument pur fondé sur la superfluidité de spin dans le $^3$He-B superfluide. Nous montrons que les ondes de précession de spin se propageant sur le fond des supercourants de spin dans un canal entre deux condensats de Bose-Einstein de magnons sous forme de domaines à précession homogène imitent les propriétés de l'horizon noir/blanc. Une fois l'horizon de trou blanc formé, bloquant la propagation des ondes de précession de spin entre les deux domaines, nous avons observé un effet d'amplification, c'est-à-dire que l'énergie des ondes de précession de spin réfléchies par l'horizon est supérieure à l'énergie des ondes de précession de spin excitées avant la formation de l'horizon. De plus, la température estimée du rayonnement de Hawking spontané dans ce système modèle est d'environ quatre ordres de grandeur inférieure à la température de fond du système, ce qui en fait un outil prometteur pour étudier l'effet du rayonnement de Hawking spontané.
title: Magnonic Analogue Black/White Hole Horizon in Superfluid $^3$He-B: experiment
